platform.branchable_state: only manifest-declared, disposition-reviewed surfaces and operations

database.note: Each key of engines is a claimed database engine and its value the min-inclusive/max-exclusive version line that engine is claimed on; an engine this map does not name is refused (platform_database_engine_unsupported) rather than compared against another engine's range, and each version diagnostic names its engine because the range is now a function of the engine. There is deliberately no verified series map here, unlike the php and wordpress axes: each entry already names exactly one measured line, and the engines map already forces an engine-by-engine decision, so a third series map would prevent no failure. MariaDB 11.x is pinned by the sandbox harness's own Docker tag (mariadb:11 -- see sandbox/db.yml, sandbox/docker-compose.yml); verified live: 11.8.8-MariaDB as of this writing. MySQL is pinned to exactly the 8.4 LTS line the harness boots (mysql:8.4 -- sandbox/db.mysql.yml:60, selected with DUO_DB_ENGINE=mysql); the max stops at 8.5.0 rather than 9.0.0 on purpose, because a wider bound would admit innovation series nobody ran. Verified live 2026-08-24 on MySQL 8.4.11 (mysql:8.4, the LTS line the harness boots): regress_core_scope_database.sh green on both engines in a single run -- authentication, named-lock bounds, promotion-lease acquire/renew/release, a planted non-JSON lease row failing closed, ledger schema and collation, and a real round trip with verified zero-write repeat, byte-identical recapture and a passing doctor row per engine, with cross-engine schema and refusal-envelope diffs recorded -- plus regress_core_data_boundary.sh and conformance-core both green under DUO_DB_ENGINE=mysql. The source-level MySQL 8.4 dialect audit of every SQL construct the agent sends (docs/mysql-dialect-audit.md) preceded that run and its five probe groups are that suite's assertions verbatim. If the live matrix fails, the remedy is to drop the MySQL entry and restore a MariaDB-only engines map, never to widen around a failure.

php.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's exact Docker tags: each key of verified is a PHP feature-release series, and its value is the exact patch a full live proof ran on (8.3 on wordpress:7.1-php8.3-apache / wordpress:cli-php8.3 -- sandbox/tests/live/regress_core_scope_platform.sh, regress_core_data_boundary.sh, conformance-core). The series map exists here for the same reason it exists on the wordpress axis: this range spans two PHP feature releases (8.3, 8.4), each its own migration with its own deprecations, so a bare range would claim a line nobody ran. Verified live 2026-08-24: regress_core_scope_platform.sh ran both series in one solo run -- core 7.1 on PHP 8.3.33 and on PHP 8.4.24, the 8.4 cell booting wordpress:7.1-php8.4-apache / wordpress:cli-php8.4 by digest and asserting the booted PHP_VERSION equals the 8.4 value here exactly -- and regress_core_data_boundary.sh and conformance-core are green on those same 8.4 digests. If the live matrix fails, the remedy is to drop the 8.4 entry and restore max 8.4.0, never to widen around a failure. A runtime is accepted only when it is inside [8.3.0, 8.5.0) AND its MAJOR.MINOR is one of those exercised series, so an unexercised minor line inside the range is still refused rather than claimed by a bare range. Note that today verified names every series the range contains, so the map narrows nothing operationally right now; it is the shape that makes the next widening a data edit plus one exercise cell instead of a re-argued claim. Patches inside an exercised series are claimed on exactly the basis MariaDB 11.x already is here -- one measured runtime per line. There is no last_verified on this axis: nothing in this tree reads a newest-PHP scalar, and an invariant with no reader is decoration.

wordpress.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's exact Docker tags: each key of verified is a core series, and its value is the exact patch a full live proof ran on (6.9 on wordpress:6.9.2-php8.3-apache, 7.0 on wordpress:7.0.3-php8.3-apache, 7.1 on wordpress:7.1-php8.3-apache @sha256:65919a9ca10940feb10d9400fead0d639bf86241f47c91e2b9ea4703aa8452cf -- sandbox/tests/live/regress_core_scope_platform.sh, regress_core_data_boundary.sh, conformance-core). The 7.1 value is the literal two-component string WordPress itself ships for that series' first release (wp-includes/version.php:19 reads $wp_version = '7.1'); that is what get_bloginfo('version') returns and what this gate compares, so "7.1.0" would name a WordPress that does not exist. Verified live 2026-08-24: the 7.1 matrix cells are green (core 7.1 round-trips, repeats with zero writes and recaptures byte-identically on PHP 8.3.33 and 8.4.24, and out-of-window artifacts refuse typed with zero mutation), and regress_core_data_boundary.sh and conformance-core are green on the 7.1 proof image; the source-level 7.1 audit of every assumption manifests/core.json makes preceded the run. If the live matrix fails, the remedy is to drop the 7.1 entry and restore max 7.1.0 / last_verified 7.0.3, never to widen around a failure. A core is accepted only when it is inside [6.9.0, 7.2.0) AND its MAJOR.MINOR is one of those exercised series, so an unexercised minor line inside the range is still refused rather than claimed by a bare range. Patches inside an exercised series are claimed on exactly the basis PHP 8.3.x and MariaDB 11.x already are here -- one measured runtime per line. last_verified is the newest exercised core and the one sandbox/pair.yml boots by default.
